html:
The Terena are an Indigenous people of Mato Grosso do Sul in western Brazil, speakers of an Arawakan language. They are one of the larger Indigenous peoples of the state.

Their ancestors were part of the Guaná peoples of the Chaco in what is now Paraguay, farmers who lived alongside the horse riding Mbayá. In the 1700s and 1800s they moved east across the Paraguay River into Brazil. They fought on Brazil's side in the Paraguayan War of 1864 to 1870, then lost much land to cattle ranchers. Today many farm, and many work in towns; they have pressed hard to recover their lands. Their neighbours to the north are the Bororo.
sum: The Terena are an Indigenous people of Mato Grosso do Sul in western Brazil, speakers of an Arawakan language. They are one of the larger Indigenous peoples of the state.
